result.title: Investigating the effects of the patch size in Time Series Foundation Models
result.summary: Patch size is a central design choice in patch-based time-series foundation models, controlling temporal resolution, sequence length, and computational cost. We study how this choice interacts with transformer architecture through a controlled comparison of encoder-only and decoder-only forecasting models trained with the same data mixture and optimization budget. Across 97 GIFT-Eval tasks, encoder-only models consistently benefit from smaller patches, whereas decoder-only performance follows a U-shaped trend, with an intermediate patch size performing best in aggregate. Dataset-level results further show that the preferred decoder patch size increases with the forecasting horizon. For encoder-only models, increasing context length improves performance across patch sizes, although the gains diminish beyond a context length of 2048. Finally, training-compute and CPU-latency Pareto analyses reveal complementary regimes: decoder-only models provide efficient low-cost alternatives, while encoder-only models attain the highest overall accuracy. These results show that the choice of patch size and architecture should be made depending on the forecasting horizon and deployment constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 在相同数据混合与优化预算下受控比较 encoder-only 与 decoder-only 时间序列基础模型，跨 97 个 GIFT-Eval 任务考察 patch size 与架构、预测期长、上下文长度的交互，并给出计算与 CPU 延迟的 Pareto 分析。
AI.relevance_reason: patch size 实为「分辨率—序列长度—算力」的折中，与视觉 token 粒度如何保留细节、以及精度/成本权衡可能有类比，可供核查；但该文属时间序列预测，不涉及 latent 推理状态，借鉴或仅停留在粒度与预算设计层面。
